title: The Night the Power Went Out
source: Original passage written for this demonstration (no ReadWorks content)
content:
It started with a loud crack of thunder. Then the lights flickered, the refrigerator stopped humming, and the whole house went dark.

"Nobody move," said Dad. "I will find the flashlight."

Nora and her little brother Eli sat very still on the couch. Outside, the rain pounded the windows. Eli pulled a blanket up to his chin.

"I don't like the dark," he whispered.

"Neither do I," Nora admitted. She had said she was brave all week, but right now her heart was beating fast.

Dad came back with a flashlight and a box of candles. Mom found matches in a kitchen drawer. Soon the living room glowed with a soft, golden light, and the shadows on the walls seemed friendlier.

"We have no television and no computers," said Mom. "What should we do?"

Eli had an idea. He held the flashlight under his chin and made a spooky face. Everyone laughed, even Dad. Then Nora showed them how to make shadow animals with her hands. A rabbit hopped across the wall. A bird flew above the bookshelf. Eli's dog, which looked a little like a duck, made everyone laugh again.

Later, Mom made hot chocolate on the camping stove, and Dad told the story of the biggest storm he remembered from when he was a boy. Nora listened with her chin on her knees. She noticed that she had stopped feeling afraid.

When the power finally came back on, the lights blazed and the refrigerator started to hum. Nobody cheered.

"Can we leave the candles for a few more minutes?" asked Eli.

Dad smiled, and Mom nodded. They sat together a little longer, listening to the rain grow softer until it stopped.
